subject: Decision Making
title: Moneyball and Data-Driven Decisions
description: One-minute skill: Moneyball and Data-Driven Decisions.

hook.text: In 2002, the Oakland A's used statistics to build a winning baseball team on the league's smallest budget.

buildup.text: Traditional scouts relied on intuition: how a player looked, his build, his swing. Billy Beane trusted numbers instead.

discovery.text: Beane found that on-base percentage predicted wins better than batting average. The market undervalued patient hitters.

twist.text: The A's won 20 consecutive games. But they never won a championship. Data optimizes averages, not playoff luck.

climax.text: Moneyball proved that data beats intuition for repeatable decisions but still cannot control single random events.

punchline.text: Stats beat scouts for seasons. Playoffs are still luck. Data has limits.

quiz.question: What key insight did Moneyball's data approach reveal?
options: On-base percentage predicted wins better than traditional stats
